evidence: 2026 check: no qualifying event has occurred this year - the worst 2026 drawdown was ~9% spread over a MONTH (late Feb-late Mar Hormuz crisis), not 5 trading days, and it was recovered in ~11 sessions
2026-10-23: index at 7,623.68 after a ~3% reversal from the 7,844 record; ~46 trading days remain in the window
2026-10: stress indicators elevated - oil +6% on the week to $103 WTI on possible US strikes on Iran, Fed decision Oct 28, US midterms, 84% of index members already in correction
Historical conditioning: all 5-day >10% crashes occurred amid pre-existing drawdowns or exogenous shocks (war escalation and an oil spike are live candidates)
40289.strongest_opposing_case: Conditions rhyme with crash precursors: record concentration, dot-com-level CAPE, an oil/war shock brewing, narrow breadth, and April 2025 proved a >10% 5-day crash can arrive from a policy headline in days - the unconditional base rate understates current hazard.
40289.reasoning_summary: Unconditional base rate ~1.5% per 2.2 months. Multiply up ~3-4x for live risk factors (oil shock + possible US-Iran strikes, extreme valuations, narrow breadth, momentum reversal) as such regimes historically concentrate crash probability. Even stressed, a 5-day -10% remains rare: final 0.06.

base_rate.reference_class: Frequency of NYC losing >=8 net billionaires year-over-year on Forbes city counts
base_rate.source: Forbes city-count history: NYC went ~110 (2024) to 123 (2025); net city drops of 8+ occur mainly in major bear-market years (2009, 2022-style), roughly 1 in 5 years

evidence: 2025-04: Forbes 2025 city ranking: NYC #1 with 123 billionaires (threshold: Yes requires fewer than 115 in 2026, i.e. a net loss of 9+)

2026-04: Forbes 2026 World's Billionaires list set records - 3,428 billionaires globally (+400 YoY), $20.1T combined wealth - a strongly billionaire-additive year that mechanically favors city counts rising

2026: Mamdani-exodus narrative is loud (commentators predicting moves to FL/TX/TN) but no measured billionaire departures are documented; Fortune's analysis notes threatened exoduses over progressive mayors historically did not materialize
Caveat: a separate Forbes-cited figure of 111 NYC-primary-residence billionaires circulated in late 2025, showing count methodology varies and adds resolution uncertainty
KXNYCBILLIONAIRES-26-115.strongest_opposing_case: If resolution uses a 'primary residence' methodology similar to the 111 figure cited in late 2025, the count may already sit below 115; Mamdani's first-year tax agenda gives the wealthy both motive and time to redomicile to Florida before any year-end snapshot.
KXNYCBILLIONAIRES-26-115.reasoning_summary: Base rate for an 8+ net city loss is ~20% and 2026 was a record billionaire-creation year (+400 globally, markets +12% YTD), which pushes counts up, not down. Offsetting: methodology ambiguity (111 vs 123 style counts) and a genuine politically-driven relocation narrative. Net: stay near base rate at 0.20.

base_rate.reference_class: P(ND Sep-Dec average output >= ~1,176 kbpd given Jan-Aug 2026 actuals summing to ~277.6M bbl of the 421.101M threshold)
base_rate.source: NDIC/EIA monthly series: Aug 2026 run-rate 1,161 kbpd rising ~3-5 kbpd/month, but ND Nov-Dec weather historically cuts output 2-5% in roughly half of years

evidence: 2026-10-20: ND August production 1,161 kbpd (+3 vs July); 2026 monthlies: Jan 1,124.8 / Feb 1,133.6 / Mar 1,142.7 / Apr 1,141.4 / May 1,125.0 / Jun 1,152.8 / Jul 1,157 / Aug 1,161 kbpd
Arithmetic: Jan-Aug total ~277.6M bbl; remaining 122 days need ~143.5M bbl = ~1,176 kbpd average Sep-Dec, i.e. ~15 kbpd above the August rate sustained through winter
2026-08: state DMR said sustained drilling and robust crude prices should support output; the state's 1,150 kbpd revenue forecast has been exceeded in recent months
2026-10-23: WTI at $103 gives operators maximum incentive to complete wells into Q4, but ND November-December blizzards routinely knock 20-60 kbpd off monthly averages
KXNDKOIL-27FEB26-T421.101.strongest_opposing_case: Output is trending up ~4 kbpd/month into $100+ oil - Sep/Oct could print 1,170-1,185 kbpd, and a mild early winter (as in 2023) would carry the Sep-Dec average past 1,176 comfortably, resolving Yes.
KXNDKOIL-27FEB26-T421.101.reasoning_summary: Threshold demands Sep-Dec average ~1,176 kbpd vs Aug's 1,161. Price incentive ($103 WTI) argues for continued growth; ND winter weather argues for Nov-Dec dips below trend in most years. Central path lands at ~418-421M bbl - essentially a coin flip shaded No by winter risk and EIA-vs-state data wobble: 0.42.
